rules.description: Removing or changing a declared interface (route, tool, topic) needs its contract updated.
rules._why: 31 interface declarations found.

rules.description: A code change of 30+ lines comes with a test change.
rules._why: 4606 test files import production code here, so the convention exists.

rules.description: Changes stay reviewable.
rules._why: Large changes get shallow reviews.

rules.description: Structural debt never grows: layer violations, dependency cycles, dependencies not in the model, hidden dependencies, components no test imports, model check errors.
rules._why: Locks today's counts so they can only go down. Run --baseline after accepting.

rules.description: Components depend downward through the model's layers: Build, tests and lint rules → Entry points → Workbench → Editor → Platform → Base.
rules._why: The model orders 6 layers; this keeps new code from importing upward.

rules.description: Base is the bottom layer: it imports nothing from platform, editor, workbench, sessions or the entry points.
rules.fix: Move the shared piece down into base, or invert the dependency with an interface the upper layer implements.
rules._why: VS Code's instructions: a layered architecture from base, platform, editor, to workbench.

rules.description: Platform services do not import the editor, the workbench or the agents window.
rules.fix: Define the service interface in platform and implement it higher up.
rules._why: VS Code's layered architecture.

rules.description: The editor (Monaco) does not import the workbench or the agents window; it ships on its own.
rules.fix: Expose an editor contribution point and register from the workbench side.
rules._why: Monaco is published separately, so it cannot depend on the workbench.

rules.description: The workbench never imports the agents window (src/vs/sessions); sessions may import the workbench, not the other way round.
rules.fix: Put what both need in the workbench (or lower) and import it from sessions.
rules._why: Stated in VS Code's instructions: sessions may import from the workbench but not vice versa.

rules.description: Code in a common folder runs everywhere, so it imports nothing from browser, node or electron folders.
rules.fix: Keep the environment-specific part in browser/ or node/ and pass it in.
rules._why: VS Code's environment layering: common, browser, node, electron.

rules.description: Browser code imports nothing from node or electron-main folders; it must also run on the web.
rules.fix: Reach node capabilities through a service with a node implementation.
rules._why: VS Code runs in the browser as well as Electron.

rules.description: Built-in extensions use the extension API, never VS Code's own sources.
rules.fix: Use the vscode API, or propose an API.
rules._why: Built-in extensions run in the extension host against the public API.

rules.description: No @ts-ignore or @ts-nocheck: a type error is fixed, not hidden.
rules.fix: Fix the type, or narrow it with a guard.
rules._why: Hiding a type error defeats the type check the fence runs.

rules.description: No new `any` in a type annotation or cast.
rules.fix: Give it a real type or interface.
rules._why: VS Code's instructions: do not use any or unknown unless absolutely necessary.

rules.description: No new types or values in the global namespace.
rules.fix: Export it from a module and import it where needed.
rules._why: Stated in VS Code's instructions.

rules.description: Open editors with IEditorService, not IEditorGroupsService.activeGroup.openEditor.
rules.fix: Inject IEditorService and call openEditor on it, so revealIfOpened and preserveFocus apply.
rules._why: Stated in VS Code's instructions: it bypasses the editor-opening logic.

rules.description: Localized text uses placeholders ({0}), never string concatenation.
rules.fix: localize('key', "Text {0}", value)
rules._why: Concatenated strings cannot be translated correctly.

rules.description: Use an arrow function instead of .bind(this) to keep `this`.
rules.fix: () => this.method()
rules._why: Stated in VS Code's instructions.

rules.description: No .only in a test file: it silently skips every other test.
rules.fix: Remove .only before committing.
rules._why: A focused test turns the rest of the suite off without failing.

rules.description: No debugger statements.
rules.fix: Remove it.
rules._why: Left-over debugging pauses every developer's run.

rules.description: Tests do not stub a global object through an any cast; the dependency is made injectable instead.
rules.fix: Add an optional constructor parameter that defaults to the real implementation and pass a fake in the test.
rules._why: Stated in VS Code's learnings.

rules.description: At the top level, write export function name() rather than an exported arrow function.
rules.fix: export function name(...) { ... }
rules._why: Named functions read better in stack traces.

rules.description: Every new source file starts with the Microsoft copyright header.
rules.fix: Copy the header from any existing file in src/vs.
rules._why: Stated in VS Code's instructions.

rules.description: A change to the root package.json comes with package-lock.json.
rules.fix: npm install, then commit package-lock.json.
rules._why: A dependency change without its lockfile installs something different in CI. A warning, not a block: on 8 of 483 merged commits the root package.json changed without the lockfile (scripts or metadata, not dependencies).

rules.fix: Run npm run install-fast in the worktree.

rules.description: An agent never force-pushes.
rules.fix: Push new commits; a person decides history rewrites.
rules._why: A force-push can drop a reviewer's commits.

rules.description: A proposed API file (vscode.proposed.*.d.ts) changes together with the proposals registry, extensionsApiProposals.ts.
rules.fix: Update the version or entry in extensionsApiProposals.ts (npm run gulp compile-extensions-build regenerates it).
rules._why: The registry lists every proposed API and its version; a change to one without the other breaks extensions that use it. A warning, not a block: 4 of 483 merged commits edited a proposed API file without the registry (comments and docs).
